meta.title: Annora — Your whole school year, in one place
meta.description: Classes, students, grades, attendance and the end of the year, organised and always at hand. For secondary-school teachers in Argentina.

hero.title: Your whole school year, in one place.
hero.lead: Annora replaces the loose spreadsheets in Drive. Classes, students, grades, attendance and the end of the year, organised and always at hand, on your computer or your phone.
hero.note: All you need is a Google account. No new passwords.

pains.title: Sound familiar?
pains.lead: One spreadsheet per class, another for attendance, averages worked out by hand and, in December, hunting for who owes the subject.

items.after: All your classes and schools in one place
Each term's suggested grade, already worked out
Attendance on your phone, with each student's percentage

items.before: In December, hunting for owed subjects
items.after: The end of the year and owed subjects, listed for you

how.title: From the first class to the end of the year, in three steps.

steps.title: Sign in with Google
steps.text: No new passwords. Your data belongs to your account and nobody else sees it.

steps.title: Set up your classes
steps.text: School, subject, year and class days. Add your students, or bring them over from last year in one tap.

steps.title: Use it every class
steps.text: Take attendance, add tasks and scores. Annora works out averages, flags what's missing and puts the end of the year together.

features.title: Built for how teaching works in Argentina.
features.lead: Terms, the 1 to 10 scale, the passing grade, school-wide days off and owed subjects: Annora already knows them.

groups.title: Know each student
items: Groups that come on different days
Adaptations, with their own version of each task

groups.title: The year under control
items: School calendar with holidays and days off
Term grades with their expected range
Closing the year and owed subjects

groups.title: Time back
items: Works on your phone and computer

attendance.title: Take attendance with one hand.
attendance.text1: Everyone starts present: you only tap whoever was absent or late. Holidays and days off already show as days without class, and if there was a strike, you mark it with its reason.
attendance.text2: Each student has their percentage, and if it drops below the minimum you choose, their average tells you.

data.title: What happens in your classes stays between you and your classes.

points.title: Only you see your classes
points.text: Each teacher sees only their own: their schools, classes, students and grades.

points.title: Your students don't need an account
points.text: They're your records, not users. Nobody has to install anything or sign up.

points.title: Adaptations without diagnoses
points.text: What's stored is which content is adapted, never a diagnosis. The label only says “Adaptation”.

items.a: The first month is free; after that, it's a monthly subscription of USD 2.

items.q: Do I have to install anything?
items.a: No, everything works in your browser. You can even install it and use it like an app.

items.q: Do my students have to sign up?
items.a: No, all the records are yours: your students don't need an account.

items.q: Does it work if I teach at more than one school?
items.a: Of course! You can add several schools, classes and students. Each school has its own calendar, and each class its own class days.

items.q: Can I use it in English?
items.a: Yes, it's a multilingual platform: it's in Spanish and English today.

meta.title: Privacy policy — Annora
meta.description: What data Annora uses, what for, where it is stored and how to ask to see, correct or delete it.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data Annora uses, what for, where it is stored and what you can do about it. It is written for teachers, who are the people who use Annora. The Spanish version is the one that applies.

sections.title: Who is responsible
paragraphs: Annora is a project by Federico Atadia, a teacher in Argentina, who is responsible for the data described here.
For any question about your data, write to {email}.

sections.title: What Annora receives from your Google account
paragraphs: Annora has no passwords of its own: you sign in with your Google account. When you do, Google shares your name, your email address and your profile picture with Annora, and nothing else. Annora does not ask for access to your Gmail, your Drive, your contacts, your calendar or any other data in your account.
That data is used only to identify you when you sign in and to keep what you enter tied to your account. It is not used for advertising, it is not sold and it is not shared with anyone.
Annora's use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
You can remove Annora's access to your Google account at any time from {google}.

sections.title: What you enter in Annora
paragraphs: Annora stores what you enter: your schools and their calendar, your classes, your students (name, grades, attendance, notes and adaptations), your tasks and their files, and your preferences.

They are your records as a teacher, as your spreadsheets were: you decide what to enter and are responsible for having it. Annora keeps them to show them to you and nobody else: no other teacher or person can see them.

Your students have no account in Annora and Annora never contacts them. For adaptations, what is stored is which content is adapted, never a diagnosis. Please don't enter diagnoses or other health data.

sections.title: Where it is stored
paragraphs: Annora runs on two services: Supabase, which stores the database and files and handles signing in with Google, and Vercel, which serves the application. Their servers may be outside Argentina. They only process the data so that Annora works.
Everything travels encrypted (HTTPS), and Annora only lets each teacher see and change their own data.

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: Annora only uses the cookies it needs to work: your session, and the ones that remember the language, light or dark theme, colour and menu. It uses no advertising or analytics cookies, and no third-party tracking tools.

sections.title: How long it is kept and how to delete it
paragraphs: Your data is kept while you use Annora. You can ask for a copy, a correction, or for your account and everything you entered to be deleted, by writing to {email}. You get an answer within 10 business days, and a deletion is completed within 30 days.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under Argentina's Personal Data Protection Law 25.326 you can access your data and ask for it to be corrected, updated or deleted.
You may exercise the right of access free of charge at intervals of no less than six months, unless a legitimate interest is shown, as set out in article 14, paragraph 3 of Law 25.326.

Argentina's Agency for Access to Public Information (Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública), as the supervisory authority under Law 25.326, handles complaints from anyone whose rights under the personal data protection rules are affected.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If this policy changes (for example, when Annora starts charging a subscription), the new version is published here with its date, and important changes are announced in the application before they apply.
